newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Carso Q1 hit by lower prices.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Carso Q1 hit by lower prices.

text.p: Mexican holding company Grupo Carso S.A.'s first quarter earnings and margins are forecast to fall following the company's price cuts on leading cigarette brands, analysts said.
"We'll all be looking out for the effect of lower cigarette prices," said Shayne McGuire, an analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico.
Grupo Carso's cigarette division Cigatam announced on February 21 it had cut prices on its Marlboro and Marlboro Light brands by 20 percent to counteract the tide of contraband sales in Mexico.
"The most interesting thing to look out for in this quarter's results should be Cigatam's performance," Goldman Sachs analyst Kerry McHugh wrote in a recent report.

"We estimate that a 30-percent increase in Marlboro volumes would would compensate for the price cut," she added, noting the company had yet to give strong indications this increase had been achieved.
A survey of three analysts showed they predicted net earnings per share of 0.85 pesos for the first quarter.

Several analysts declined to offer estimates saying there were too many unknowns entailed in making projections, such as the cigarette price cuts and striking miners returning to work, both of which took effect about half-way through the quarter.

Analysts also noted corporate restructuring would limit the validity of year-ago comparisons. Grupo Carso hived off its telecommunications and insurance holdings last year, into Carso Global Telecom and Seguros Inbursa, respectively.
Grupo Carso also announced its cable-making arm Grupo Condumex said on March 19 it planned to buy a majority stake in competitor Conductores Latincasa.
Robert Hulme of Interacciones in New York said he was not including earnings by Latincasa in his overall estimates "as they have not actually signed on the dotted line yet."
Hulme added he expected some negative impact on Grupo Carso earnings from lower cigarette earnings, but this would to some extent be offset by Condumex, the group's largest subsidiary.
